intro: Armenian media today highlight developments in mining policy, environmental cooperation, and cultural figures, with multiple outlets covering government statements on industry standards and international environmental agreements.

topics.title: Armenia pushes for higher standards in mining sector
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan emphasized the need to align Armenia’s mining industry with the highest possible standards. This was echoed by a ruling party MP who urged abandoning extremes in the sector, while the CEO of Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine affirmed mining’s continued role as a driving force of the economy.

topics.title: Armenia and Kyrgyzstan deepen bilateral cooperation
topics.text: Armenian and Kyrgyz leaders signed a joint statement and cooperation documents across various sectors. The Kyrgyz president invited Pashinyan to the second Global Mountain Summit 'Bishkek+25', and officials commented on newly established sister-city relations between Yerevan and Bishkek.

topics.title: Armenia advances environmental cooperation on transboundary lakes
topics.text: Armenia’s environment minister explained the memorandum on protecting Lakes Sevan and Issyk-Kul, outlining its envisaged measures. The UNESCO Director-General also visited Armenia, meeting officials and touring the Zvartnots Cathedral.

topics.title: Armenia sees new opportunities from COP17 participation
topics.text: Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan said COP17 will create new opportunities for international cooperation for Armenia. Parliamentary Speaker Alen Simonyan added that the conference also holds political, economic, and security significance for the country.
